title: Has anyone got AI to make a character hold weapons properly? 48 to do, stuck
author: DiligentIngenuity291
selftext:
UE5, character on a Mixamo skeleton, 40 weapons + 8 consumables.

I tested Opus 5.5, Fable 5.2, Astra 6.2 and Gemini Neon. None of them gets a hand onto a weapon correctly.

What I tried (see image):

1. **Procedural** (find the grip on the mesh, IK the hands, close fingers by contact): fingers inside the weapon, broken wrists.
2. **AI image -> mocap**: ChatGPT image of the character holding the weapon, then RGB MoCap (ExMR) onto my rig. Posture and hand shape are good, but the hands land 15 cm off the weapon and the barrel is 19° off.
3. **Posed by hand in Blender**: the only one that looks right, far too slow for 48.

Also tried text-to-motion (Kimodo in UE 5.9): useless for weapon gestures.

Fallback plan, the classic way: \~8 hand poses per grip type, two sockets per weapon, left hand by IK.

* Any AI tool or pipeline that actually gets hand-object contact right?
* If not, what's the fastest way to author the grip poses and sockets?

Thank you

comments.author: Simple-Law5883
comments.body:
huh, i can't really tell you much, just that fable 5.2 absolutely doesn't have an issue with this for me. Usually i just give it references of people holding guns, let it itterate until it's done with a very strict reviewer and after successfull completion i let it write a skill.. I am currently not working on a gun, but this is also quite difficult. This was done by modeling the hand first, i had fable 5.2 do a deep research on how professional artists model hands, then it transformed the hand and weighted the verticies for rigging. What i can see in your screenshot is that the rig overall needs to be remade. Your shoulder and arm weights aren't good enough to do a gun holding position.

My recommendation: Rerig elbows and shoulder and then have fable 5.2 plan it out in detail before doing anything else. And references.

replies.author: Rick_Stoner_
replies.body:
Yeah, I’ve run into weird animations with Mixamo too. For the left wrist twist, I’d check the wrist and forearm bone orientations and how the animation is being retargeted.

I had a character dragging one foot in-game, and the fix ended up being the walk clip. I switched to the walk animation made for that model, trimmed it to the steady part of the stride, enabled Loop Pose, and locked root XZ so the network movement system handled moving the character. Now I check the exact clip that’s playing, make sure it’s the regular walk cycle, and test it in-game before touching the rig.

I like your idea for equipped gear too. I’d start with a grip point on the weapon, use IK to line up the hand, and pose the fingers around the grip. A separate target for the trigger finger could help if you need that extra precision.

Use Claude at least opus but preferably fable and it will do a very good job. Tell it don’t stop until it’s as close to one to one Match as possible.
